about: Château Talbot is named after John Talbot, the English commander who retook Bordeaux in 1452 and died at the Battle of Castillon in 1453, though no record shows he owned the land. The name was already on 18th-century maps, and the estate was ranked a Fourth Growth in 1855. Désiré Cordier began buying it in 1917 and reunited the property. It has stayed with his descendants ever since, now Nancy Bignon-Cordier and her family.

Talbot is one of the Médoc’s largest single estates, about 110 hectares in one block in the heart of Saint-Julien. It lies on one of the area’s highest gravel rises, up to 23 metres above sea level, over limestone. The grand vin comes mainly from the higher gravel of the plateau. The 2010 was fermented in wooden vats and aged in barrels, half of them new, and it is about 62% Cabernet Sauvignon, a third Merlot and a little Petit Verdot.

2010 was an outstanding Médoc vintage, and Talbot’s is one of its best recent wines. Critics note crème de cassis, plum, licorice, roasted herbs and smoke. It is full-bodied and fleshy, with deep, ripe tannins and a long finish. Decanter and James Suckling each scored it 94, and Wine Enthusiast 93. At fifteen years old it is entering its drinking window.
facts: About 110 ha in one block on hilltop gravel
